title: I might not be natural
summary: A fake-apology opening becomes an attack on fake natties: NH says he has never taken steroids but 'might not be natural' because no fitness YouTuber can prove natural status. Fake natties killed trust, spread steroid culture to kids and made natural bodybuilding a lost cause, and the natty-or-not hunt only makes them stronger. His answer is to ignore them, stop watching evasive creators, and judge advice by testing it yourself.
claims: He 'might not be natural' only because no one on fitness YouTube can prove it; he has never taken steroids
The default on fitness YouTube has flipped: ten years ago creators were assumed natural, now anyone claiming natural is presumed a fake natty
Nothing any fitness YouTuber says, him included, can be fully trusted, because the community has been betrayed too many times
Blowing up on fitness YouTube largely involves drugs; naturals struggle to compete, which pushes naturals to take drugs too
Fake natties killed trust: they gathered followers while posing as natural, then admitted use; burned viewers never trust again and the rest forgive them out of attachment
Teenagers who have never taken creatine know steroid cycles in detail; he calls this knowledge toxic because it replaces innocence
When he started training he didn't know what steroids were and thought whey protein was a steroid; that naivety is what let him last
Watching fake natties makes viewers jaded: they decide the physique is unreachable without drugs and their self-esteem collapses
Natural bodybuilding is dead: most competitors on stage at natural shows aren't natural, and the golden age won't come back unless drugs disappear
Fake natties also killed good information by replacing it with practices that only work for drug users
Natural claims are a catch-22: claim natural and people say a real natural wouldn't need to; stop claiming it and they say you didn't state it, so you aren't
Blood tests prove nothing for a YouTuber: a scheduled test can be waited out, and nobody is surprise-testing creators
Urine tests are even weaker because most drugs clear within a day or two; only random testing works, and YouTubers test on their own schedule
Judging natural status by looks depends on the viewer's standards; ordinary people would call his physique unnatural
Muscle biopsies may reportedly reveal current or past use, but past use allows lies by omission; some creators claim natural while off cycle
Openly enhanced creators now look more honest than naturals, even though many of them lied about being natural years earlier
The natty-or-not hunt backfires: fake natties don't suffer from accusations, while accused naturals have no defense because you cannot prove a negative
Fake-natty hunting channels increase fake natties' visibility, like an exterminator whose house fills with more roaches
Fitness YouTube content now revolves around drugs, which is worthless knowledge for natural lifters
Natural status is an enigma with no answer; hunting for clues wastes your focus and hands fake natties the attention they want
Fake natties can't be eliminated because they come from human nature; naturals should ignore them and build their own path
Stop watching creators who play coy about natural status or make 'am I natural' videos; clicks give them power
Don't give in to 'no one is natural' nihilism: it implies drugs don't affect results, and drug users' advice doesn't work as well for naturals
Judge any advice, his included, by applying it yourself; being hurt by a creator's betrayal shows fanboy attachment
Natural bodybuilding can be reborn through individuals working outside organizations and conventions
